description: REQ-105's monitoring-plan function, computeColdStartRepaymentRate({loanRows, n=20}), is defined as operating 'over the first n (by issued_ms ascending, across ALL borrowers colony-wide) loans whose ORIGINATING row had successfulOnTimeRepayments === 0 at issuance (i.e. every borrower's own first-ever loan)' -- but this parenthetical equivalence ('i.e. every borrower's own first-ever loan') is FALSE under the spec's own other rules, and the spec never specifies the actual algorithm needed to compute the real definition. REQ-105's own Edge Cases state: 'A late-but-eventual full repayment (REQ-109: on_time=false) does NOT increment successfulOnTimeRepayments -- the borrower's next loan cap stays exactly where it already was.' Combined with REQ-102's 'at most one outstanding loan at a time' rule (a borrower can only get a NEW loan after their prior one reaches 'repaid'), this means a borrower whose FIRST loan was repaid LATE still has successfulOnTimeRepayments=0 when their SECOND loan is issued -- so their SECOND loan is ALSO, by REQ-105's own formula, issued at the cold-start cap (computeLoanCapUsd(0)=$0.02) and would ALSO satisfy 'successfulOnTimeRepayments === 0 at issuance.' 'Cold-start loan' can therefore recur multiple times for the SAME borrower (any time all of that borrower's prior loans were repaid late, never on-time) -- it is NOT equivalent to 'every borrower's own first-ever loan,' contrary to the spec's own explicit parenthetical claim. Neither loans.jsonl's own row schema (as described piecemeal throughout the spec: loan_id/lender_id/borrower_id/principal_usd/repaid_usd/total_due_usd/status/on_time/issued_ms/due_ms) nor computeColdStartRepaymentRate's own description specifies whether 'successfulOnTimeRepayments at issuance' is (a) a NEW field snapshotted onto each row at issuance time -- never introduced or mentioned anywhere else in the schema -- or (b) something the function must RECOMPUTE by walking each borrower's own loan history in issued_ms order and re-deriving what countSuccessfulOnTimeRepayments would have returned using only that borrower's own prior rows. Since computeColdStartRepaymentRate's own signature takes only flat {loanRows, n} with no borrower-stratification step described, an implementer is left to invent this non-trivial recomputation algorithm from scratch, with a real risk of silently implementing the FALSE 'first-ever loan' equivalence the spec's own parenthetical asserts, systematically undercounting genuine repeat cold-start loans (a late-repaying borrower's second, third, etc. cold-start-cap loan) from this monitoring metric that REQ-105's entire 'experimental hypothesis, honestly tracked' framing depends on for its own credibility.

evidence.snippet: over the first n (by issued_ms ascending, across ALL borrowers colony-wide) loans whose ORIGINATING row had successfulOnTimeRepayments === 0 at issuance (i.e. every borrower's own first-ever loan) ... A late-but-eventual full repayment (REQ-109: on_time=false) does NOT increment successfulOnTimeRepayments -- the borrower's next loan cap stays exactly where it already was

crossCheck.note: computeColdStartRepaymentRate's signature ({loanRows, n=20}) and its PROP-105f fixture (3 repaid + 1 defaulted + 1 active) never demonstrate or test the multi-cold-start-loan-per-borrower case the spec's own REQ-105 edge cases logically imply is possible, and never specify whether the 0-at-issuance fact is a stored row field or a recomputed derivation.
